editorial:
You're dropped into 1950s Hollywood, where studio fixer Eddie Mannix spends his days putting out fires. When star Baird Whitlock vanishes from the set of a big biblical epic, Eddie has to track him down while juggling a pregnant actress, a singing cowboy, and a group of communist writers who claim responsibility. The whole thing feels like a love letter to old Hollywood, packed with goofy set pieces and big-name cameos.

The cast is stacked, with Josh Brolin anchoring everything as the exhausted but loyal Mannix, and George Clooney hamming it up as the kidnapped star. The Coen brothers keep things light and silly, though the story jumps around so much that it can feel scattered. If you enjoy old-school movie magic and dry humor, this is a fun ride. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Eddie discovers the communist writers are holding Baird at a Malibu beach house. After a tense standoff, Baird is returned to the studio unharmed. Eddie turns down a lucrative job offer from Lockheed to stay in Hollywood, choosing his chaotic but beloved film world. The movie ends with him walking back onto the lot, ready for the next crisis, as the biblical epic finally wraps filming.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood and dry comedy.
